phys-astro-01-c2.text: David Weinberg, Ohio State University Department of Astronomy. Lecture 8: Principles of Stellar Structure III. Nuclear Energy. Ohio State University Astronomy.
phys-astro-01-c2.quote: The mass of a helium nucleus is 6.643x10-24 g, 0.7% lighter.
phys-astro-01-c2.claim: The mass deficit is ~0.7% of the original hydrogen mass

phys-astro-01-c2.text: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center, Imagine the Universe. Life Cycles of Stars (X-ray spectra lesson background). NASA Imagine the Universe.
phys-astro-01-c2.quote: Creating heavier elements through fusing of iron thus requires an input of energy rather than the release of energy.
phys-astro-01-c2.claim: Iron is the most stable nucleus, so fusion beyond iron costs energy rather than releasing it.
